images.prompt:
Create one original premium photorealistic field-guide portrait of an anonymous mature Chortai (Hortaya Borzaya). Text-only factual synthesis, no input photograph or named source dog likeness.

One mature strong lean Chortai (Hortaya Borzaya), choose male about70cm within RKF65–75cm. Functional long flat muscles and strong bones, square to slightly rectangular body, no excessively fragile greyhound caricature. Dry elongated wedge head with moderately broad skull and equal-length long real muzzle, weak smooth stop, thin lips, black nose and ordinary dark oval oblique eyes. CRITICAL Chortai ear anatomy from RKF: natural LONG THIN NARROW slightly pointed ear leathers set at outer eye level, almost as long as the muzzle. In this relaxed pose both leathers are laid BACK FLAT lengthwise along the upper neck, extending rearward behind the jaw; the near leather must be plainly readable as a long narrow soft pointed strip beside the upper neck. These are not short triangular sideways flaps and not compact rolled rose ears with exposed inner bases. No laterally flaring rose folds, erect or semi-erect ears, rounded short hound flaps, cropped ears or short button folds. Preserve long narrow hanging-back anatomy, not an ear shape averaged from other sighthounds. Long muscular moderately high neck, strong straight back, fairly long broad slightly arched loin, long gently sloping wide croup, deep oval chest nearly to elbows and defined waist tuck. Long strong straight lean forelimbs and muscled well-angled hindquarters, four complete compact oval arched paws. Short straight elastic coat up to2.5cm, choose independent warm fawn with restrained white lower chest/toes and dark nose, no speckles or long Borzoi hair. Full natural long low-set slender saber-shaped tail carried down in relaxed stance with gentle open upward curve near its free tip; complete root/course/endpoint visible, no kink, tight corkscrew, sharp raised vertical tail or docking.

Invent a fresh relaxed standing right-facing three-quarter pose, head turned slightly toward viewer enough to show the long near ear laid back flat beside the upper neck, mouth closed. A broad clear dry steppe footpath in southern Russian countryside, subdued tawny grasses distant and soft cool morning light. Entire developed adult head/ears/trunk, four distinct coherent complete leg courses and all four grounded paws, believable joints/weight/contact shadows. Entire natural low attached tail through free endpoint separately readable against clear space. Do not copy the researched grey-white broadside named specimen, rear reed-wall yard, exact markings, terminal ring arrangement, pose/expression/hair or lighting.

One dog only, no puppy, fragile emaciation, long Borzoi hair, rose ears, rounded hound ears, cropped ears, docked/stump/kinked tail, tight tail corkscrew, missing/fused/extra limbs, collar, leash, people, quarry, other animals, hunting gear, props, text, logo, watermark or border. profileEvidence.summary: Calm in its general temperament, the Chortai becomes sharply focused when game comes into view. This southern Russian sighthound combines speed with stamina, and uses scent as well as sight to find quarry. Its working rhythm shifts from a leisurely walk or trot to a full gallop during pursuit.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: A calm, keen-eyed Russian sighthound that pairs speed with stamina and uses its nose as well as its eyes when hunting.
profileEvidence.author: L worker C

sourceSnapshots.evidence: RKF current Hortaya Borzaya standard approved14September2022: Purpose describes hunting hare/fox/small ungulates, speed with endurance and scent during search. Behavior/temperament states calm temperament with a well-developed visual reaction, leisurely trot or walk before quarry rises and full gallop in pursuit. Historical overview describes breeding in southern Russia. These are breed-standard descriptions, not individual safety, suitability or performance guarantees. The same standard explicitly says this breed is not recognized by FCI; do not confuse FCI group placement with recognition.
